newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Thermo to keep on acquisition path.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Thermo to keep on acquisition path.

text.p: Thermo Instrument Systems Inc's purchase of Britain's Life Sciences International Plc for 236 million stg on Tuesday is its biggest buy yet but is unlikely to mark the end of the U.S. firm's acquisitive ways.

"We are in discussion with a number of companies all the time, some in Europe, some in the U.S, some in the Far East," Earl Lewis, executive vice president and chief operating officer of Thermo Instruments told Reuters in an interview.
"At any point in time there are anywhere up to 30 or 40 companies that we are actively watching."
Thermo launched its second major purchase in the UK with a recommended cash bid for Life Sciences of 135 pence per share in the scientific equipment firm.
Last year the U.S. company bought British Pharmaceutical company Fisons Plc's worldwide scientific instruments division for 202 million sterling.
"Up until now, Fisons was the largest acquisiton we had ever made and that has worked out well and made us even more bullish on the idea of acquiring more companies," said Lewis.
Thermo Instruments is a public subsidary of Thermo Electron Corp.
It develops, manufactures, and markets instruments used to detect and measure air pollution, radioactivity, complex chemical compounds, toxic metals and other elements.

Thermo said Life Sciences' manufacturing, distribution and service base will help it extend its product offerings into new markets such as clinical laboratory equipment and will enhance its presence in the bio-analytical instrumentation marketplace.

Riccardo Pigliucci, chief exexcutive of Life Sciences, told Reuters in an interview: "Thermo is now expanding into the laboratory equipment markets and clinical markets and is looking at Life Sciences as the seed company to expand in that area."
Life Sciences intends to declare a second interim dividend, in place of any final dividend, for the year ended December 31, 1996 of 3.0 pence per share.

The offer together with the second interim dividend represents a premium of around 49 percent to Life Sciences' closing share price on Monday. By 1109 GMT, shares in Life Sciences had roared ahead 40-1/2p to stand at 133p.

Thermo, which is 82 percent owned by Thermo Electron and has market capitalisation of around 3.2 billion dollars, said that the acquisition will be financed from its cash resources and expects the purchase to enhance earnings straight away.
